cells.tense: You have hold of something that came out of a change, and you know it's worth keeping exactly as it is.
cells.ask: offer your way of seeing in trade for someone else's, and let what they hand back change the shape a little — what returns will steady the hold, not loosen it.
cells.core:
You can see how something works — the pattern under all the particular cases — and you haven't rushed to flatten it into rules or drag it back into examples. It sits in you steady. You hold it the way you'd hold a thing that's still becoming itself, careful and unhurried, and that patience is the whole of what makes the hold good. Not every insight has to be spent right away. Some need to be lived beside until they're true at the bottom.

Keep that, and when someone offers something back, take it. Receiving is what keeps a hold from hardening. A thing held in one set of hands only, forever, slowly stops being what it was.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape of it and you hold it steady — let what someone gives back steady the hold.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, keeping it steady until it can be shared
cells.place: in the pattern under things, where the shape shows through without any of the stuff it's made of

cells.tense: You're bracing against a change that hasn't arrived, measuring out how you'll keep things once it lands.
cells.ask: let one person tell you what they actually feel, instead of sketching their feeling for them beforehand — that opens the hold again.
cells.core:
The pattern is still there and you can still see it, but you're leaning forward past it — rehearsing how the shape will hold when the next change comes, and the one after that. What you have now gets drafted into defense against a future you'll fix in place before it grows. The seeing is still accurate. The arrangement is out ahead of the life.

Someone across from you is feeling something right now that no pattern predicts. Be in touch with that as itself — not as the case that will confirm the shape. That contact, felt and honored both ways, is what lets the hold breathe again.
cells.sheetLine: You're protecting the shape against a future you can't write yet — let someone real tell you what they feel.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, keeping it steady until it can be shared
cells.place: in the pattern under things, where the shape shows through without any of the stuff it's made of

cells.tense: You stopped at a threshold that has already passed, still holding a shape the change left behind.
cells.ask: put one actual thing you want where another person can see it, and defend the wanting — direction comes from being genuinely moved, not from pushing feeling into the pattern.
cells.core:
You can still see how things work under the surface, and you still keep what the changes left — but the keeping has gone quiet. A judgment sits in you unspoken, a shape you'd defend if called, and no one is being called. The pattern is not gone. The relationship to it went still.

One thing you actually want, named and stood behind, is what gets you back. Not the pattern defended in the abstract — one thing in the world you're moved toward, said plainly to a person, and stayed with when it meets friction. Direction won't come from staring harder at the shape. It comes from being moved and moving.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped at the door and kept holding — pick one thing you want and stand behind it.
cells.verb: holding what the change produced, keeping it steady until it can be shared
cells.place: in the pattern under things, where the shape shows through without any of the stuff it's made of

cells.tense: You're already holding what came out of the change, and you're talking about the holding as if it were just how things are.
cells.ask: say plainly what you're keeping, and out of what — and notice the moment you choose to hold it, because that choice is the structure, and it's yours.
cells.core:
You see the pattern under things and you keep it steady — that's your hand at work, and it's been yours the whole time. But when you talk about it you make it sound like the shape is holding itself, like the stability is just the situation. The work keeps running; the credit doesn't.

Pick one thing you're keeping — a shape, a way of seeing, a piece of what a change left — and say out loud what it is and out of what you're keeping it. Naming what you hold brings the authority back to where it started, which is you, and the structure starts making sense in your presence again.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the pattern and calling it the weather — say what you're keeping and own the keeping.

cells.place: in the pattern under things, where the shape shows through without any of the stuff it's made of
